summary: The drawing pad runs a real small convolutional network with stored trained weights. Its test-set result reproduces the displayed 97.0%. The separate 7 diagram uses real filtering and pooling but prepared final digit scores.

claims.claim: The drawing pad runs convolution, ReLU, pooling, dense scoring, and softmax.
claims.how: An independent tensor implementation matches every layer on ten samples and 64 random drawings to absolute error below 1e-10.

sources.title: Convolutions for images
sources.says: The usual neural-network convolution operation slides a learned kernel using cross-correlation.

sources.title: Pooling
sources.says: Max pooling keeps the maximum value within each local window.

claims.claim: The network reads 8-by-8 images from a named digit dataset.
claims.how: The asset identifies UCI Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits; pixel values are scaled from 0–16. All ten stored samples classify correctly.

sources.title: Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits
sources.publisher: UCI Machine Learning Repository; Alpaydin and Kaynak
sources.says: The data contains 8-by-8 digit images with pixel values from 0 to 16 and a separate test file.

claims.how: The exported network correctly classifies 1,743 of 1,797 original UCI test rows: 96.99499%, which rounds to 97.0%.

claims.note: The tolerance is display rounding to one decimal percent. It is dataset accuracy, not a promise for arbitrary handwriting.

claims.how: The 3-by-3 cross-correlation and ReLU produce a 5-by-5 map. Max pooling includes smaller windows at the edges.

simplified: The introductory diagram uses one fixed filter on a 7-by-7 sample, a normalized feature map, partial edge pooling windows, and stored digit scores. The drawing network reads 8-by-8 grayscale pixels and does not retrain while drawing.
